notes.title: Where this was run
notes.text: T3 Code server 0.0.46-nightly.20261008.2849 (CLI 0.0.46-nightly.20261007.2787) on Linux (desktop build), not the macOS nightly named in the design brief. Every conformance thread used runtime mode full-access, inherited from the build thread. One top-level thread per provider, as authorised; each case and repeat was a separate message with a fresh clone of the fixture branch. Driver messages are verbatim in each transcript.md.

notes.title: Child-write probe (REQ-ISOLATION)
notes.text: A live delegated imps run from the build thread (parent claudeAgent/claude-opus-5-5) pinned one writer to each child-capable provider. The core created sibling worktrees under ~/.local/state/t3-plugins/imps/worktrees, dispatched each probe with delegate_task, and read each marker itself: codex, claudeAgent, opencode and antigravity children could all write outside the parent checkout (with full-access runtime). Evidence: conformance/probes/0.0.46-nightly.20261008.2849/. The Antigravity child noted that its tool refuses a working directory outside the workspace roots, although writes there succeed.

notes.title: Live delegation and cancellation (REQ-LIVE-T3)
notes.text: conformance/live-t3/cancel-probe.json: a wait-mode delegate_task returned a fenced t3-result block; an async child running `sleep 600` was cancelled with task_cancel, which answered cancel_requested; task_status then showed interrupted / result_available / no pending child runs, which the adapter treats as the confirmed stop. In the matrix, Claude children twice reported waiting_for_children and the parents treated it as not a result.

notes.title: Parent provider switch within one thread (REQ-LIVE-T3)
notes.text: In the Claude conformance thread, run 20261009-142158-6ce8d6 dispatched a survey child under claudeAgent; the thread was then switched to antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash-high with t3_thread_configure and asked to resume. The core recorded `provider_switch: parent provider claudeAgent -> antigravity` and accepted the new provider's capabilities under the same parent thread ID; see conformance/results/.../claudeAgent/provider-switch/.

notes.title: Defects the matrix found (fixed after the matrix, at the PR head)
notes.text: 1. Review and read-only briefs showed a changed_files example, and a Codex reviewer listed the files it reviewed there; the core rejected the claim and blocked two Antigravity bug-fix repeats. Read-only briefs now show `"changed_files": []` and a stray list gets one correction round. 2. A child cited evidence relative to its own working directory (children inherit the thread's scratch folder, not the clone); briefs now require absolute evidence paths and a relative path that does not resolve gets one correction round. Both have regression tests in tests/test_review_regressions.py::MatrixFindingsTest.

notes.title: Grader change
notes.text: The pending-task grader first required exactly one dispatched round. Claude repeat 1 legitimately had a second round: the core's one correction round after a malformed first result, with its own clientRequestId. The check now requires exactly one *initial* dispatch and a distinct clientRequestId per round, which is the property the case tests (no duplicate dispatch after interruption).

notes.title: Interventions and infrastructure
notes.text: Interventions counted: one (an operator message 'try it again' in the Claude thread at 13:46:51Z). An earlier operator message ('what next', 13:11:10Z) arrived after a repeat had completed and did not affect it. Infrastructure retries, not counted as model behaviour: the OpenCode thread (three attempts, session never opened) and one Codex parent turn that failed to start.

notes.title: Observed but not adopted
notes.text: This T3 build injects agent instructions that mention an ACP fallback transport and exposes link_pull_request, watch_pull_request and preview tools as standalone MCP tools. At plugin 0.1.0, the version this ledger records, imps was limited to the pinned orchestrator doc's surface (link_pull_request as a t3_thread_update action, no PR watcher, preview tools found by description) and did not call them. imps 0.2.0 adopted link_pull_request, watch_pull_request and unwatch_pull_request; the ledger has not been re-run since.

notes.title: Usage and cost
notes.text: T3 does not expose token usage or cost to the parent at this version, so usage/cost is null for every repeat. usage.json in each repeat records the run's active-budget seconds.

notes.title: Plugin version
notes.text: 0.1.0+ga50f506cd178 is the installed snapshot every matrix repeat ran on. The final PR head adds the round-3 review fixes and two matrix-found fixes on top of it (see the other notes).

notes.title: Row fields
notes.text: `starting_revision` lists the distinct fixture base SHAs that provider's repeats started from, in run order (each repeat used a fresh clone of the fixture branch, so a row can carry several); it is empty when no case run started. `child_write_probe.source` names the single probe run all rows share: run 20261009-121018-0f6d5d, plugin 0.1.0, base 7008f23c6ca6340cbc753c4494d7547f9618d021, evidence in conformance/probes/0.0.46-nightly.20261008.2849/.
